rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.

This differs from the licensed 'Lean pass'/'Emphasis pass' provenance headers on L52/L56, which the rule explicitly carves out because they anchor a still-binding constraint; this row narrates a completed audit diff instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L46: "**What happened:** A one-screen gap map across memory / verifier / skill and one stale rule cut in place." Three-move read: (1) count+noun — 'A one-screen gap map... and one stale rule cut' (matches the canonical noun-phrase-fragment shape of the rule's own examples, e.g. 'One plan, two reads'); (2) qualifier on shape — 'across memory / verifier / skill'; (3) lands on destination — 'in place' (edited into the existing rules file, not left hanging). Grep tell `^\*\*What happened:\*\* You` does not match (sentence opens on 'A', not 'You'), so this isn't the banned replay shape. Past-tense check: the block is a noun-phrase fragment with no finite verb, same shape as the rule's own canonical examples, so the past-tense requirement doesn't apply to it any more than it does to 'One SKILL.md'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned for the four shapes. No empty negation ('X, not Y' against an unheld prior). No deictic drumroll ('That is the X' with no real antecedent). No bold-label-echo (every bold widget label — Time/Session/What you do/What you build/The point/What happened — is chrome per module-shape convention, never restated as the following sentence's subject). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'three to five items' (L30) and 'One rule cut, no more' (L44) both specify a target SIZE for an artefact the student is about to produce through conversation, not a numeral duplicating a visible adjacent list already on the page — the rule targets restating a count the reader can already see in bullets below, which doesn't occur here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L13: "**The point:** two sessions are enough to place every lesson." 'every lesson' is the superlative tell this rule targets. Applying the rule's own cheapest-counterexample-source test (the file's own contingency plan): the maintainer's own failure-mode list two sections down names 'Packaging over-credit — student treats the packaged run as fully solved and skips the what packaging missed beat' and 'Rule-cut dodge — student accepts every rule still holds without testing it against the diagnosis' — both admit the two-run diagnosis does NOT automatically place every lesson, only that it CAN, contingent on the student's own rigorous pushback. That is a real tension between the flat claim and the file's own fallback. Countervailing: the backing block's Stance ledger (L106-108) already frames this as a deliberate 'house position, carried as position' with a stated would-move-it condition, which suggests the maintainer has already weighed this — so I'm surfacing it as a rule question rather than an obvious defect: is 'every lesson' meant to be read as scoped to this training's own two-run design (licensed by §21's 'artifact/corpus we control' carve-out) or as a general epistemic claim (which the file's own failure modes contradict)? If the former, the maintainer may want the line to say so; if the latter, the superlative should go.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either scope the line to the training's own design ('two sessions are enough to place what this exercise is built to catch') or drop 'every' and let the sentence stand on the concrete instance; do not hedge it into mush.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: L43-44, three short sentences all on the same idea (scope discipline — cut only one rule): 'Claude may pause... just say go' / 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged... Claude may rewrite more' / 'One rule cut, no more.' The third sentence is a four-word terse closer, not a restatement at a different altitude — it reads as a memorable, compressed reinforcement of a genuinely risky scope-creep moment (an in-place edit to a config file), not padding. Elsewhere (L34-35) the file cleanly follows the concrete-instance-plus-one-generalising-sentence shape and stops.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap language ('you're missing X', 'you already think you're using X'). No ability-tier assumption ('at your scale', 'for a beginner'). No tourist/practitioner-style identity-criterion split anywhere in body. The one pre-prompt readiness check (L7: deciding whether the M5 session 'is done enough, should be stopped, or counts as the partial artefact') is plausibly-failable at this exact point — M5's send-off may genuinely still be running — and is exactly the 'fresh state from previous phase' the rule keeps as legitimate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.

Naming matches the shared-library convention `<file-slug>-<n>`.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's fence uses `m4/` and `m5/` branch names ('the un-packaged session's are in task.md, its m4/ branch...') — this is exactly the rule's own worked example of legitimate grounding (branch namespace, not a curricular event label with no in-session referent).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read both fences in isolation from body: P1 fully specifies both session locations, coordinate files, and the four-dimension ask without relying on body callouts. P2 fully specifies what to read, what to find, what to do in the null case ('If every rule still holds under diagnosis, say so and stop') entirely inside the fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 is already split into scene-setting / read-instruction / four bulleted dimensions / closing-rank paragraphs. P2 is split into read / find-and-cut / report-and-null-case paragraphs. Both pass the read-aloud diagnostic; no >2-move paragraph left unsplit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1: body lead-in (L22, 'Ask Claude to read both sessions side by side...') mirrors P1's fence opening move ('Read both. Start with both session transcripts...') — same verb (read), same noun-phrase (both sessions/both) — this half passes cleanly. P2: body lead-in (L37, 'Ask Claude to cut one rule the two-session diagnosis killed...') opens on 'cut', but P2's fence opens on 'Read ./CLAUDE.local.md and this session's scrollback...' — verb and noun-phrase don't rhyme (cut/one rule vs Read/CLAUDE.local.md-and-scrollback). The lead-in summarises the fence's dominant OUTCOME rather than mirroring its literal first clause.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either open the lead-in on the fence's actual first move ('Ask Claude to read CLAUDE.local.md and this session's scrollback, then cut...') or accept the outcome-summary framing as intentional — low severity since the fence is read in full immediately after regardless.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt's frontmatter declares `permission-mode:` (confirmed by direct read of both registry files); correct, since neither prompt's behaviour depends on a specific mode — both are default-mode conversational asks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 runs in a fresh/cold session per the Session widget ('new, "Module 6 worktree session"') and is correctly self-contained (carries its own file paths, branch names, artefact descriptions). P2 runs warm, same session, no `/clear` between P1 and P2, and correctly back-references scrollback ('this session's scrollback: the gap list I just ranked') rather than re-specifying context. 40b check: 'the gap list I just ranked' / 'the dominant gap' are genuinely in-scrollback referents (Claude itself produced them answering P1, refined via the L28-30 pushback exchange), not curriculum-coined phase labels absent from the agent's context. No concurrent-worktree hazard (40a): this exercise opens one worktree, no fork.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2's write instruction ('Cut it from ./CLAUDE.local.md in place') is not followed by an unconditional STOP that could block it; the only 'stop' ('say so and stop') is explicitly conditional on the null case (no rule earned cutting), so it never competes with the write instruction for the last-imperative slot.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's four-dimension structure is content structure the teaching moment depends on (already established under check_student_facing §6), not a padded formatting spec (no 'clear title, a Rules section, plain markdown' style trailing template). P2's 'two sentences' is a minimal conciseness constraint, not padding.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This exercise's shape is a solo diagnostic + rule-cut with the student's own agent — closest to 'Solo retro with Claude' (private learning extraction), a deliberate, appropriate choice for an individual mid-module beat (group_beat_markers: false per body-view signals, no forced default to a group/pair mechanic without reason).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer L68 states the target mood ('practitioner fluency — "I know how to test, I know how to learn."') and its two watch-fors (compliance-feel, credibility-performance). Body's tone (direct, evidence-grounded, no paperwork-feel) is consistent with the target and doesn't slip into either watch-for; the one mechanical/setup beat (L7) is correctly mood-exempt under the rule's own setup-vs-teaching diagnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: H1 ('Map the gaps, cut the rule') and all `##` headers lead with diagnostic/constructive framing (map, diff, read, cut, say go), not a failure-branded word (fabrication/violation/hallucination); 'gaps' names an unaddressed area, not a punitive failure label, so this doesn't read as a discipline-named-after-its-failure-mode title.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
